title: VNHSGE: VietNamese High School Graduation Examination Dataset for Large Language Models
extended_summary:
This paper introduces VNHSGE, a Vietnamese High School Graduation Examination dataset created to evaluate large language models (LLMs) on educational tasks. The authors argue that existing benchmarks are dominated by English-language data and do not adequately capture the breadth, difficulty, and linguistic features of Vietnamese high school exams. As a result, they build a new benchmark spanning nine subjects and including both multiple-choice questions and literary essay tasks.

The dataset combines official and illustrative exam questions from the Vietnamese Ministry of Education and Training and similar exams collected from public sources. It includes 19,000 multiple-choice questions and 300 literature essays, with accompanying answers and step-by-step explanations. The paper describes the dataset structure in detail, including subject coverage, difficulty levels based on Bloom’s taxonomy, bilingual Vietnamese-English versions, and JSON/Word formats designed for LLM testing and evaluation.

The study evaluates ChatGPT and BingChat on the dataset and compares their performance against Vietnamese students’ score distributions. The main finding is that these LLMs reach human-level performance in some subjects and question types, especially literature, English, history, geography, and civics, but remain weaker on mathematics, physics, chemistry, and biology. The paper’s contribution is primarily a benchmark and evaluation resource, not an intervention study on learner outcomes.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI’s GPT-based conversational LLM/chatbot used for question answering, explanation generation, and translation.
identified_tools.use_case: Used alongside BingChat to evaluate performance on the VNHSGE dataset; also used to translate the Vietnamese dataset into English and to generate answers/explanations for test items.

findings.finding_summary: ChatGPT performed at a human level in a number of areas, including literature and English, when evaluated on the VNHSGE dataset. The paper reports that it could handle knowledge and comprehension level questions, but it struggled with complex calculations and multi-step reasoning; no sample size, effect size, or confidence interval is reported.
findings.measure: Accuracy on VNHSGE subject exams and question types

findings.finding_summary: On the literature dataset, ChatGPT was described as capable of responding to literary queries and generating essays. The paper indicates human-level performance in literature overall, but does not provide quantitative outcomes for reading comprehension or writing measures.
findings.measure: Literature reading comprehension and essay-writing performance

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: Generic generative AI / large language model chatbot used for text generation, question answering, and translation.
identified_tools.use_case: The paper discusses LLMs generally as educational tools and as candidates for evaluating reading comprehension, writing, and question-answering tasks, without studying a non-named generic system separately.

quality_tier_rationale: This is a dataset/benchmark paper rather than a direct evaluation of an educational intervention with rigorous causal design. It reports descriptive performance comparisons of ChatGPT and BingChat, but no experimental evidence, effect sizes, or learner-outcome study on K-12 reading/literacy improvement.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper suggests generative AI can answer literature and English items at a human level, but provides no direct evidence of improvement over business-as-usual or non-AI supports. Because no effect sizes are reported and the evidence is benchmark-style rather than instructional, the impact on learner outcomes is unclear.
